title: WAF, bot and anti-automation evasion
status: AUTHORED. The offensive half of the defence mirror. Every entry states which defence level it addresses.

atom_notes.A15: evasion starts by measuring which defence is actually deployed, not by assuming one
atom_notes.A05: the mutation is a shape or encoding change that one layer normalises and another does not
atom_notes.A03: client identity is the boundary when the defence is behavioural
atom_notes.A07: rate is a resource on both sides, and pacing is the control that keeps a test legal
atom_notes.A08: challenge solving and browser driving exist to make the client look like what it is not

required_cells.why: identify the defence before choosing an evasion, or you are guessing
differential testing across client profiles is the only honest method
the payload path when the defence is protocol aware rather than signature based
prove the bypass with a control request that the defence does block
report the detection cost, since a bypass that alerts is not a bypass
defence drift, a WAF rule set changes weekly

entries.name: wafw00f
entries.role: Fingerprint the WAF, which determines which evasion class applies at all
entries.note: Run before payload selection, never after. The WAF decides which mutation axis matters.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: curl_cffi
entries.role: Browser TLS fingerprint from python, the library route past JA3 and h2 checks
oracle: a response the plain client did not get
detected_by: client JA3 not matching the claimed browser
entries.note: The comparison is the test: same request, one plain client and one impersonating. If the answers differ, the defence is fingerprinting.

entries.name: curl-impersonate
entries.role: The same idea from the shell, for quick differential checks
oracle: differing status or body versus plain curl
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: tls-client
entries.role: Go backed python client with selectable browser profiles
oracle: response only obtainable with a specific profile
detected_by: client JA3 not matching the claimed browser

entries.name: playwright
entries.role: A real browser engine driven by script, the honest bot workflow
preconditions: a script and a browser install
oracle: a flow completed that a plain request could not
entries.note: Set human timing deliberately rather than randomly. Random is itself a signal.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: undetected-chromedriver
entries.role: Patched driver that avoids the usual automation flags
oracle: page loads where headless chromium was refused
entries.note: Still detectable, just less obviously. Treat success as evidence about the defence, not as invisibility.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: cloudscraper
entries.role: Solves only the classic Cloudflare JS challenge
preconditions: a host with the old challenge
oracle: the challenge bypassed and content returned
entries.note: If it fails, that is data about the defence, not a tool bug. One attempt per host, then stop.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: chromium
entries.role: A real browser and a CDP target, which is also how REA inspects a page
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: mitmproxy
entries.role: Intercept and replay with control over the exact bytes, including pacing
oracle: exact request replay with modified framing
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: ffuf
entries.role: Fuzzing that survives rate limits by being paced, not by being fast
oracle: results inside the rate budget without tripping the limiter
entries.note: Set -rate. An agent that ignores rate turns a test into a denial of service.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.role: Template checks with rate limiting and known WAF friendly options
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: Awesome-WAF
entries.role: The WAF corpus: fingerprints, bypass notes and per product behaviour. 7,662 stars and still maintained
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: HackTricks
entries.role: Per defence technique reference with current bypass context
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: GoTestWAF
entries.role: Measures WAF detection coverage with a scoring report, the honest way to characterise a defence
preconditions: an authorised target with a WAF
oracle: score per attack class with the encoder that passed
entries.note: This is the tool that answers the detection-cost question the rest of the domain cannot. Run it once and report the score, not a bypass list.

tree.q: Which defence level are you actually facing?
tree.why: Mapped to the defence scale in the ontology: F2 signature, F3 protocol aware, F4 in app, F5 bot management, F6 identity, F7 model based. Each needs a different approach and most of them need no payload at all.

branches.action: encoding and syntax mutation against the class, one axis at a time so you learn which axis is filtered
branches.oracle: payload passes where a control is blocked

branches.action: semantic bypass, not encoding. the parser difference between two layers is the opening
branches.oracle: two layers disagree about the same request

branches.action: differential test: same request from a plain client and a real browser profile. if the answers differ, the defence is the client
branches.oracle: response obtained only with a browser shaped client

branches.a: F7 model based or rate based
branches.action: pace deliberately and keep a request budget. the goal is a result inside the budget, not speed
stop and report it. solving that is out of scope for an assessment and is a business decision, not a technical one

mirror.detect: normalisation mismatch between proxy and app
mirror.control: parse and normalise once, at the app

mirror.detect: client JA3 not matching the claimed browser
mirror.control: fingerprint the client, challenge on mismatch
limit on identity, not only on IP

gaps.gap: No tool reports the detection cost of a bypass, only whether it worked
gaps.build_candidate: attach an expected alert count per technique so a report can say what the bypass would trigger

gaps.gap: No differential harness that runs the same request across N client fingerprints automatically
gaps.build_candidate: one request, N clients (plain, curl_cffi profiles, playwright), diff the responses, emit a table
